summary: Espressif ESP32-P4 (chip rev v3.x) multimedia board with an ESP32-C5-MINI-1 co-processor for dual-band Wi-Fi 6 and BLE (the P4 itself has no radio), Ethernet, audio codec, microSD, MIPI DSI/CSI and a 40-pin J1 GPIO header.

warnings.text: 3.3 V logic at most. ESP32-P4 IO supplies are limited to 3.6 V (datasheet Table 5-1); no pin is 5 V tolerant. The 5V header pins are power only; never connect a 5 V signal to a GPIO.

The ESP32-P4 has no radio. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on this board come from the separate ESP32-C5-MINI-1 co-processor module (2.4 GHz and 5 GHz dual-band Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5 (LE) (the C5 module also supports IEEE 802.15.4)), which the P4 talks to over an SDIO bus (SD2 nets in the board schematic). The co-processor runs its own firmware and has its own programming connector; your P4 code reaches the radio through Espressif's host/co-processor software, not directly.

Chip revision: this board carries an ESP32-P4 chip revision v3.1 or later (user guide). v3.x silicon (ESP32-P4NRW16X/32X) differs from the older v1.x chips used on the end-of-life ESP32-P4-Function-EV-Board (v1.4/v1.5.2): v1.x and v3.x firmware images are not interchangeable. Build with ESP-IDF v5.5.3+ or v6.0+ and keep CONFIG_ESP32P4_SELECTS_REV_LESS_V3=n for v3.x (Chip Revision v3.x User Guide). v3.x also fixes several errata, raises the CPU to 400 MHz and adds IO hold in Deep-sleep for all IOs. Chip revision v3.1 does not support Secure Download Mode (errata ROM-770), so do not enable it. The GPIO numbering and J1 header table are the same as on the v1.5.2 board.

Strapping pins on J1: GPIO36, GPIO37 and GPIO38 (with GPIO35, which is not on J1) select the boot mode at reset, and GPIO36 also controls UART0 ROM log printing. External pull-ups/pull-downs on them can stop the board from booting. GPIO34 (JTAG source strap) is not on J1.

IO voltage domains (datasheet Table 2-1, 5-2): GPIO0-GPIO15 are LP IOs on VDD_LP (3.0-3.6 V, so 3.3 V). The HP IO banks VDD_IO_0 (GPIO16-23), VDD_IO_4 (GPIO24-38), VDD_IO_5 (GPIO39-48) and VDD_IO_6 (GPIO49-54) can each run from 1.8 V to 3.3 V (1.65-3.6 V). On this board the board schematics show VDD_IO_0, VDD_IO_4 and VDD_IO_6 on the 3.3 V rail, but VDD_IO_5 (header GPIO46, GPIO47, GPIO48, and GPIO45 if enabled) on the chip LDO output LDO_VO4 ("1V8/3V3 (SDIO)"), shared with the microSD card. Its voltage and on/off state are set by software (user guide note on LDO_VO3/LDO_VO4), so those pins may be at 1.8 V or unpowered. Check before connecting 3.3 V parts.

No GPIO is used for flash or PSRAM: the 16 MB SPI flash uses dedicated FLASH_* pins and the PSRAM is in the chip package and not pinned out (datasheet 2.7). MIPI DSI/CSI and USB 2.0 High-Speed also use dedicated pins.

On-board parts that use GPIOs not on J1: Ethernet PHY IP101GR (RMII), ES8311 audio codec (I2S), microSD card (4-bit, SD1 pins GPIO39-44), the co-processor SDIO bus, and the USB Serial/JTAG port (GPIO24/25). The codec, camera and LCD touch share the I2C bus on GPIO7/GPIO8.

GPIO26/GPIO27 on J1 are also the USB 2.0 Full-Speed OTG pins wired to the "USB Full-speed Port" Type-C; the user guide uses them as the default LCD PWM (GPIO26) and LCD reset (GPIO27) for the 7-inch display kit.

Compared with the ESP32-P4X-Function-EV-Board, J1 pins 15 (GPIO6), 32 (GPIO54) and 35 (GPIO53) are not connected by default here: they go to the C5 wake-up line, the C5 enable and the speaker-amplifier enable. Each can be moved to the header by moving a 0 ohm resistor (user guide footnotes). J1 pins 22, 23 and 40 (GPIO1, GPIO0, GPIO45) are not connected either (32 kHz crystal and SD power).

Also the on-board I2C SDA line (net ESP_I2C_SDA in the P4X-C5 schematic v2.0), shared with the ES8311 audio codec and the camera/LCD connectors. Usable as I2C SDA for extra I2C devices on the same bus; do not use it as a plain GPIO if you use the codec, camera or touch screen. Voltage: LP IO domain (VDD_LP, 3.3 V). Physical J1 pin 3.
